evidence.observed_facts: Four school vacations are stored for MOE Kindergarten, primary and secondary schools, plus the four scheduled school holidays printed in the same release and the three designated days off-in-lieu for schools (9 February, 3 May and 27 December). The 27 December designation falls inside the end-of-year vacation and is recorded as a separately printed closure, not an extra vacation day. Pre-university end-of-year vacation differs: JC Year 1, MI Year 1 and MI Year 2 end on 27 November 2027; JC Year 2 and MI Year 3 end with the GCE A-Level examinations. Those differences are recorded here, not duplicated as overlapping rows.
evidence.source_role_note: School layer covered: MOE Kindergarten, primary and secondary; pre-university dates differ and are noted, not stored as a second overlapping layer.

currency_assumptions: All venue prices are published in SGD. Every USD comparison figure uses the European Central Bank reference rate served by the Frankfurter API for 2026-11-24: 1 SGD = 0.77526 USD, rounded to the nearest whole US dollar.
An hourly or day rate is converted with its published hire span recorded in price_detail; a window the rate does not cover is not inferred.
A per-person or per-session price is recorded as published and is not multiplied out to an 8 h or 12 h package unless the page states the span.
The soft budget is USD 5,000; exactly USD 5,000 is not over budget, and cost is never a gate.

alcohol.quote: Class 1B Supply of liquor (all types, including beer) for consumption at the licensed premises stated in the liquor licence 0600hrs to 2200hrs One Year $660; Class 2A Supply of beer only ... 0600 to 2359hrs ... $460; Class 5 Temporary licence where licence is required for a short period of time, such as once-off events and exhibitions ... 1 day $22
alcohol.source_locator: Liquor Licence Category and Fees table
alcohol.source_title: Singapore Police Force — Types of Liquor Licences and Fees

value.class_1b: All liquor including beer, at the licensed premises, 06:00-22:00.
value.class_2a: Beer only, at the licensed premises, 06:00-23:59.
value.class_5: Temporary licence for one-off events: 1 day S$22, up to 30 days.
value.event_window: A 09:00-21:00 event with beer at 19:00-21:00 sits inside the Class 1B (to 22:00) and Class 2A (to 23:59) trading hours.
value.licence_required: Supplying liquor requires a licence unless exempted; a 50-person mixer serving beer therefore depends on either the venue's own licence or a temporary licence.
value.open_question: Which entity supplies the beer - venue, caterer or organiser - decides whether the venue licence or a Class 5 licence applies. No licence is implied here.
value.public_entertainment: Transmission of recorded music in hotels, offices and shopping centres is exempt from the Public Entertainments Act; the exemption conditions for scheduled activities end at 22:30, and anything outside them needs a Police or IMDA licence.

food.quote: Generally, food businesses must be licensed to prepare and sell food to consumers ... Retail businesses selling food items that have a higher food safety risk and/or settings that pose greater risks in view of the scale of its operations (e.g. catering businesses) are required to be licensed by SFA.
food.source_locator: When does SFA require a licence/permit?
food.source_title: Singapore Food Agency — businesses that need a food retail licence

value.caterer_licensed: A catering business preparing the mixer dinner must hold an SFA food retail licence.
value.no_licence_when: SFA states a licence is not required where food is not meant for sale.
value.open_question: Confirm the caterer's SFA licence and whether the venue charges a buyout or kitchen fee for outside catering.

language.quote: While Malay serves as Singapore's national language, English, Mandarin, Tamil, and Malay all maintain official language status. English is the working language and is used in schools, business, government, and on road signs throughout the city.

language.statutory_quote: Malay, Mandarin, Tamil and English shall be the 4 official languages in Singapore. (Constitution Art. 153A(1), indexed text of sso.agc.gov.sg)

value.event_material_rule: No requirement to publish this private event's materials in a second language was found; all claims in this store are in English.
value.open_question: A public-facing campaign may still need a language review; that is a publishing decision, not a venue constraint.

declared_gaps.text: 35 of 36 records resolve to building tier and one (The Working Capitol) to exact_venue; no record is street, area or unresolved. Every row carries the provider that answered, the query, the check date, the returned place, the match evidence, the response file that exists on disk and every failed lookup. Photon returned no tier match for 22 addresses, so Nominatim answered those rows; six addresses (Pico Creative Centre, 41 Beach Road, 40 Sam Leong Road, 21 Collyer Quay and the two ISCA rooms) still had no independent housenumber match and use the listing-page geotag as the building point. The ISCA postcode also differs by two digits (operator 049709, OSM 049711).

The recorded 12-hour count falls from 22 to 3. All three are the Lifelong Learning Institute rooms, whose rate card publishes facility booking hours 0800-2200 and a full-day 08:00-22:00 block. The other 19 venues that previously carried a 12-hour yes publish only a per-day hourly tariff span; that span is recorded as the 8-hour floor, not as a continuous 09:00-21:00 hire. Nine venues publish no hire interval at all.

room2f publishes Saturday as two sessions (08:00-16:00 and 17:00-23:00), so neither the 8-hour nor the 12-hour window is continuous; Synergy Room publishes a full-day session ending 17:30 with a separate 18:00-22:00 evening; The Masons Table starts at 10:00.

Photos now come from operator pages only: room galleries on the Tagvenue room listing and the Arts House Group and National Gallery room pages. They are hotlinked, not copied, and no independent licence grant is claimed. 30 venues carry at least one usable image, 20 carry four or more and 6 carry none. Of the 122 usable images, 113 are room- or floor-plan-specific and 9 are labelled centre, workspace, lobby or other fallbacks (JustCo and The Working Capitol sell no discrete hire room). Dimensions are measured from the served image files and stored per photo.

All 54 theme-by-lane cells were attempted. Four 2027 occurrences were added (Asia AI Conference, ICADS, WikiEXPO Singapore, Blockchain Festival), taking the story from 11 to 15. Luma, Meetup and AI Tinkerers printed only 2026 dates, so their yield is zero; the Eventbrite 2027 hits outside the six themes were dropped.

Blockchain Festival 2027 is stored on the organiser Eventbrite page date (9 October 2027) while confslist.com prints 27 March 2027 for the same FINEXPO series; the conflict is recorded on the row and not resolved.

Public layer is MOM 2027: eleven date rows plus the 8 February substitution day, stored with the MOM condition (a public holiday where the rest day falls on 7 February 2027) and the MOE footnote that treats it as a school public holiday. School layer is MOE 2027: four vacations, four scheduled school holidays and three designated days off-in-lieu for schools (9 February, 3 May and 27 December). 9 February and 3 May fall inside school terms; 27 December falls inside the end-of-year vacation and is stored as the separately printed designation, not counted as an extra vacation day. Pre-university end-of-year vacation starts 27 November 2027 and is recorded in coverage evidence, not as an overlapping second layer.

The Genting Ballroom 1 record previously cited https://www.rwsentosa.com/en/meetings, which returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-26. The address and capacity now cite the Marriott Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong event page for the same hotel at 2 Town Hall Link.

Several Tagvenue listings print a maximum capacity higher than the stored seated figure (for example ISCA 4-5 170 vs 100, Pico 150 vs 100, WeWork Suntec 100 vs 60). Capacities were not rewritten in this pass because the stored figures may be a specific layout; the difference is recorded rather than silently reconciled.

760 claim objects (608 venue, 152 event) are present with neither a source_locator nor a capture: about, display_name, lifecycle, source_url, transit and the amenity/price-basis fields, together with the nested evidence, blocker and history records that copy them. That total is the round-1 count of 750 (598 venue + 152 event) plus 10 pre-refresh blocker records deliberately preserved in venue history so their claim ids are not lost. They are listed here as lost citations rather than dressed with keyword matches: 258 top-level venue field claims are annotated with legacy_note; the field breakdown is about 6, booking_url 36, capacity 6, capacity_basis 36, display_name 36, language_support 30, lifecycle 36, price 6, price_basis 30, source_url 36. The six facts this card re-sourced (address, coordinates, access window, programme windows, holiday rows, event rows) carry either a capture and a line locator or, for the nine venues with no published hire interval, an explicit locator_note instead of an invented line.

Acceptance criterion 4 names Lovdata and Utdanningsetaten as the public and school holiday authorities, which are Norwegian. The card body and the approved plan §4 name the Singapore Ministry of Manpower and Ministry of Education, and those are the authorities read here. The Norwegian names are treated as a copy-paste conflict, not as a source instruction.

The handoff line asks for coordinate tiers for all 44 records, but the store and every other count in the card say 36 venues. All 36 existing records were assessed; no venue was added, so the reconciled total is 36.

39 URLs in the 2026-11-24 sources_consulted ledger are not carried as revision-1 ledger rows (for example the currency, weather, transit and licensing reference pages). The revision-1 ledger re-reads the event, holiday, geocode and venue lanes and records a check status and yield per row; 11 of the dropped URLs still appear as source_url on a stored claim, and the rest are list-only references. The loss is of a ledger row, not of a cited fact.
